data.gender_notes: Sharayu is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Sarayu is a river in Hindu mythology, which is considered sacred. It flows through the city of Ayodhya in the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh. The name Sharayu carries the meaning “The river Sarayu” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Sharayu usually hope their child will grow to embody the river sarayu and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of purity and divinity.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sharayu total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

historical_references.reference: Sharayu, also known as Sharada or Saraswati, is a goddess in Hinduism associated with the arts, learning, and wisdom. She is believed to be the consort of the god Shiva and is often depicted holding a veena or a book. Sharayu is also revered as a goddess of marriage and fertility.

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Sharayu is found in the Indian epic Mahabharata. In this text, Sharayu is mentioned as the name of a river that flows through the kingdom of Kashi (Varanasi) in ancient India. The river Sharayu is considered sacred and is believed to be a manifestation of the goddess Saraswati.
